content:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75+ values) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Underestimates when history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 74→70 range) — fails to recognize mean reversion.
- Tends to ignore recent low values in history when forecasting — fails to adjust downward when recent prices are near or below 70.
- Overreacts to recent high values — forecasts peak too early and too high, then drops below true value.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2 points higher than true mean for 30-day horizon — suggests bias toward higher prices.
- Model often lags in recognizing downward trends — true price drops faster than forecasted.
- When history includes a recent low (e.g., 68–70), model fails to adjust forecast downward unless preceded by a clear trend reversal.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows strong tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimates sharp reversals or spikes.
- Model overweights recent high values (last 5–7 days) and underweights distant past — leads to overconfidence in short-term momentum.
